items.title: Trump Exempts Open-Weight AI, Closed Models Face Scrutiny
items.summary:
The Trump administration has told AI developers it will not subject American-made open-weight models, like Nvidia's Nemotron, OpenAI's GPT-OSS and Meta's Llama, to voluntary safety testing, according to Reuters. The decision came the same week OpenAI disclosed another cybersecurity incident involving its models gaining internet access during testing.

In this episode of Front Page, we break down the White House's private testing discussions with Meta, Anthropic, Google, Nvidia and OpenAI, why closed models are still facing scrutiny after real breaches while open-weight models get a pass, criticism from Americans for Responsible Innovation over the lack of a published testing framework, and a letter from five Democratic senators urging Congress to make AI safety testing mandatory.

items.title: AI4Bharat at IIT Madras and Josh Talks AI Launches  India's First Independent AI Evaluation Platform
items.summary:
India has spent billions on AI models and compute but built no independent system to verify whether any of it actually works for Indians. AI4Bharat at IIT Madras and Josh Talks AI have now launched Voice of India, the country's first independent AI evaluation platform, built to test how models perform across real Indian languages, accents, dialects, and use cases rather than English-language lab benchmarks. With close to two lakh votes already collected and a goal to scale 100x, the platform aims to become the global blueprint for human-centric AI evaluation. 

In this episode of Front Page, we speak with Mitesh Khapra of AI4Bharat at IIT Madras, and Shobhit Banga and Supriya Paul of Josh Talks AI, to break down why India needs its own AI evaluator, how Voice of India tests model performance across real dialects and use cases, why benchmark independence matters as much as model sovereignty, and what it takes for trusted AI deployment at scale. 

Can owning the yardstick prove as powerful as owning the model?
